title_en: Interim Provisions on the Scope of Duties of Local Port Management Agencies

articles.content_en: 1. The local port management committee and port office are port management agencies directly under the leadership of the people's government of the province (autonomous region) or municipality where the port is located, and they shall be responsible for managing and coordinating the work of sea, land, and air ports in the region.

2. They shall be responsible for implementing the principles, policies, and provisions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council concerning port work, and shall formulate implementing rules based on the specific conditions of the port in the region.

3. They shall preside over the balancing of foreign trade transport plans for the ports under their jurisdiction, inspect and implement the transport plans issued after central balancing, and strengthen the work of forecasting and prediction.

4. They shall organize the collection and distribution work of the port, organize relevant parties to enter into economic agreements, organize the cooperation and coordination among railways, ports, and trade, strengthen the linking of vehicles, vessels, and cargoes, accelerate the turnaround of vehicles and vessels and the distribution of goods, and ensure the smooth operation of the port.

5. They shall supervise and inspect the port inspection and testing units to, in accordance with their respective duties and regulations, carry out supervision and management, as well as inspection, testing, and quarantine, of persons entering or leaving the country, means of transport, goods, and luggage and articles.

6. They shall be responsible for coordinating and handling disputes among the various port units (including foreign trade transport, shipping and cargo agency, stevedoring and tallying, warehousing and transshipment, inspection and testing, notarization and expert evaluation, foreign claims, supply and service, reception and publicity, and other relevant units), and shall have arbitration functions. The following principles shall be followed when coordinating and handling disputes among port units:
(1) Any provisions jointly issued by several departments of the State Council shall be jointly implemented. If any provision is unilaterally changed without the consent of the original issuing departments, the local port management agency shall have the right not to implement it.
(2) For disputes arising from inconsistencies in the rules and regulations among the competent departments of the State Council, the local port management agency shall promptly propose handling opinions and submit them to the Office of the Port Leading Group of the State Council for resolution.
(3) The local port management agency must strictly implement the system of requesting instructions and submitting reports for foreign-related matters arising in the course of work. For ordinary foreign-related matters that cannot be decided by the port units themselves, instructions shall be sought from the relevant units of the province (autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government) for study and handling. For major foreign-related matters, opinions of the relevant units of the province (autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government) shall be submitted together to the competent department of the State Council for study and handling. For major foreign-related matters of extreme urgency, instructions may be sought directly from the competent department of the State Council, and the relevant units of the province (autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government) shall be informed at the same time.
(4) Where there are differences in understanding among the port units in the course of work, the matter shall be resolved through consultation in accordance with the relevant state provisions, with priority given to resolving external issues. If consensus cannot be reached through consultation, the local port management agency, or the local port management agency after seeking instructions from the local people's government, shall make a decision.
(5) For conflicts and disputes concerning coordination and cooperation, the local port management agency shall promptly organize coordination, and in case of emergency, it shall have the right to make an arbitration award.
All relevant port units must implement the decisions made by the local port management agency in accordance with the above principles.

7. They shall be responsible for organizing the port units to carry out publicity and education among employees on foreign-related policies, discipline, and enhancement of public security, and shall, together with the relevant departments, inspect major foreign-related issues and serious violations of discipline at the port, and propose handling opinions.
8. They shall inspect and supervise the organization and implementation of port planning, construction, and technical renovation support work in the region, and promote their simultaneous progress.

9. They shall, in accordance with the state's policies and provisions on port opening, be responsible for the review and submission for approval of the opening or closing of first-class and second-class ports, and shall be responsible for organizing the implementation of relevant specific matters.

10. They shall carry out investigation and research, summarize and exchange experience, report to the relevant higher authorities the major conflicts and problems arising in port work, and propose solutions.
11. They shall undertake other matters assigned by the higher authorities.

12. These Provisions shall apply to the port management committees or port offices of the provinces and municipalities where first-class ports are located. The scope of duties of the management agencies for second-class ports may be prescribed by the people's government of the province (autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government) based on the specific conditions of the local port.
